title: Characteristics of PN-Junction Diode in MATLAB/Simulink

questions.q: What is the cut-in (knee) voltage of a silicon PN-junction diode?
questions.a: Approximately 0.7 V for silicon (and 0.3 V for germanium), which is the forward voltage threshold above which the diode conducts significant forward current.

questions.q: Why is a series resistor R1 always included when testing a diode's forward I-V curve?
questions.a: Because once V_D exceeds 0.7 V, the diode's impedance becomes very small; without R1 to limit current, the current would spike exponentially and destroy the diode.

questions.q: How do you extract the diode voltage V_D and diode current I_D in a PySpice DC sweep of Experiment 11?
How is the X-Y Graph block used in the Simulink model of Experiment 11?
questions.a: The Voltage Sensor across the diode feeds the X-input and the Current Sensor in series with the diode feeds the Y-input to plot I_D vs V_D directly.

questions.q: How do you simulate reverse bias characteristics in Experiment 11?
questions.a: Reverse the diode polarity (or sweep V1 across negative voltages), observing near-zero leakage current until reverse breakdown.

questions.q: How is a 1N4007 silicon diode model defined in PySpice?
questions.a: `circuit.model('D1N4007', 'D', IS=1e-14@u_A, N=1.0, BV=1000@u_V)` and instantiated via `circuit.Diode(1, 1, 2, model='D1N4007')`.

questions.q: In Experiment 11, which node is connected to the diode's anode and which to its cathode?
questions.a: Node 1 (source positive terminal) connects to the Anode, and Node 2 (resistor R1) connects to the Cathode.

questions.q: If the source voltage is 10 V, R1 = 1 kΩ, and the silicon diode drop is 0.7 V, what is the diode current?
If the plotted I-V curve is a straight line starting from 0.7 V up to 10 V on the X-axis, what mistake was made?
questions.a: The X-axis was plotted using the total source voltage V(1) instead of the voltage across the diode alone, V(1) - V(2).

questions.q: How does temperature affect the forward I-V curve of a silicon diode?
questions.a: The knee voltage decreases by about 2 mV per °C increase in temperature, shifting the forward I-V curve slightly to the left.
